headline: Trump threatens to bomb Oman if it interferes with Iran deal
summary: The US President warned that Oman would be targeted if it 'gets in the way' of a deal regarding the Strait of Hormuz, while demanding Iran surrender.
details: US President Donald Trump threatened to bomb Oman if the country 'gets in the way' of a deal with Iran concerning the control of the Strait of Hormuz.
In an interview with Fox News journalist Trey Yingst, Trump stated, 'If Oman gets in the way, we’ll bomb the s*** out of them,' referring to ongoing talks between Oman and Iran.
Trump further demanded that Iran 'put up the white flag of surrender' and reiterated on Truth Social that Iran must not be permitted to possess nuclear weapons.
Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei responded by stating that a 60-day period linked to a June memorandum between Tehran and Washington is no longer relevant.
Baghaei accused the US of violating the Islamabad MoU weeks after it was signed, signaling further tension between the two nations.
In other regional developments, the Yemeni army reported the launch of two hypersonic ballistic missiles by Houthi rebels toward the Red Sea and Mocha city.
Additionally, the KRG security agency reported that two drones targeted the office of the Kurdistan Regional Government’s prime minister in northern Iraq, though no casualties were reported.
Trump also instructed the Pentagon to substantially reduce joint military exercises with South Korea, citing high costs and Seoul's refusal to act against Iran.
caption:
Trump warns he will 'bomb the s*** out of' Oman if it blocks a US-Iran deal.

US President Donald Trump threatened to bomb Oman if the country 'gets in the way' of a deal with Iran concerning the control of the Strait of Hormuz.

In an interview with Fox News journalist Trey Yingst, Trump stated, 'If Oman gets in the way, we’ll bomb the s*** out of them,' referring to ongoing talks between Oman and Iran.

Trump further demanded that Iran 'put up the white flag of surrender' and reiterated on Truth Social that Iran must not be permitted to possess nuclear weapons.

Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei responded by stating that a 60-day period linked to a June memorandum between Tehran and Washington is no longer relevant.

Baghaei accused the US of violating the Islamabad MoU weeks after it was signed, signaling further tension between the two nations.

In other regional developments, the Yemeni army reported the launch of two hypersonic ballistic missiles by Houthi rebels toward the Red Sea and Mocha city.

Additionally, the KRG security agency reported that two drones targeted the office of the Kurdistan Regional Government’s prime minister in northern Iraq, though no casualties were reported.

Trump also instructed the Pentagon to substantially reduce joint military exercises with South Korea, citing high costs and Seoul's refusal to act against Iran.

headline_marked: Argentine legend Claudio Caniggia says [[Bangladesh is one of the best]] for its passion
headline: Argentine legend Claudio Caniggia says Bangladesh is one of the best for its passion
summary: The former World Cup star visited Dhaka to attend the Pillow Chips Dhaka Interschool Champions League 2026, praising the country's extraordinary love for football.
details: Argentine football legend Claudio Caniggia visited the Fortis Football Academy in Dhaka on Monday to serve as the guest of honour at the Pillow Chips Dhaka Interschool Champions League 2026.
The former World Cup star, known for his blistering pace and partnership with Diego Maradona, handed out prizes and spoke with the media about Bangladesh's passion for Argentina.
Caniggia expressed his admiration for Bangladeshi fans, stating that the country is 'one of the best' because of the deep emotional connection they have with the Argentine national team.
He noted that he was not surprised by the support, as he had seen images of fans celebrating victories and suffering through losses on television.
When asked about Bangladesh's chances of qualifying for the 2030 World Cup, he suggested it is a long road that depends on coaching, government support, and talent development.
The legend also shared memories of his friendship with Diego Maradona and discussed the 2002 World Cup, where he was sent off while on the bench due to a referee's mistake.
Caniggia concluded by naming Pele, Maradona, and Messi as the three most talented players in football history.
caption:
From Maradona to Messi, Argentine legend Claudio Caniggia is amazed by the passion of Bangladeshi football fans!

Argentine football legend Claudio Caniggia visited the Fortis Football Academy in Dhaka on Monday to serve as the guest of honour at the Pillow Chips Dhaka Interschool Champions League 2026.

The former World Cup star, known for his blistering pace and partnership with Diego Maradona, handed out prizes and spoke with the media about Bangladesh's passion for Argentina.

Caniggia expressed his admiration for Bangladeshi fans, stating that the country is 'one of the best' because of the deep emotional connection they have with the Argentine national team.

He noted that he was not surprised by the support, as he had seen images of fans celebrating victories and suffering through losses on television.

When asked about Bangladesh's chances of qualifying for the 2030 World Cup, he suggested it is a long road that depends on coaching, government support, and talent development.

The legend also shared memories of his friendship with Diego Maradona and discussed the 2002 World Cup, where he was sent off while on the bench due to a referee's mistake.

Caniggia concluded by naming Pele, Maradona, and Messi as the three most talented players in football history.
